subject: Private network onboarding — roles, egress IPs, and PrivateLink vs peering evaluation
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Safa Ahmed <safa@netbank.com>, networking@netbank.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-20T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private network onboarding — roles, egress IPs, and PrivateLink vs peering evaluation

Hi Safa — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the Private VPC option you were leaning toward.

Key takeaways from today's call:
- NetBank is prioritizing strict egress allowlists and isolated tenancy for the fraud detection POC (low-latency requirement, regional in us-west).
- You prefer PrivateLink if ops can manage interface endpoints inside your VPC; peering is acceptable if we can guarantee stable egress IPs and clear NAT ownership.
- Timeline: POC target week of Apr 8; procurement needs a draft SOW and pricing estimate by Apr 1.

Immediate asks we can action this week:
1) NetBank to confirm which team will own egress NAT / firewall rules (NetOps or SecOps). If NetBank owns it, we only need the allowlist; if Redwood must egress through a managed NAT we need 3 business days for routing prep and security review.
2) NetBank to share an initial list of required allowlist IPs (we proposed a small dynamic range for the PrivateLink endpoints) — placeholder CSV attached.
3) Redwood (Ben + Marissa) to model two options and hand back a short ops decision matrix: PrivateLink (endpoint ownership at NetBank) vs VPC peering (Redwood-managed egress).

I've attached a one-page preflight template (redwood-privatenet-preflight.xlsx) and a sample egress CSV to fill in (netbank-egress-ips.csv).

Next internal owners (cc'd):
- Marissa: preflight template and deployment runbook drafts
- Ben: network topology and egress IP estimate for peering model

Safa — can you confirm owner for NAT/firewall and drop the allowlist CSV by EOD Thu (Mar 22)? If that date doesn't work, propose alternate.

Thanks,
Mateo
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: redwood-privatenet-preflight.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: netbank-egress-ips.csv (csv)

Date: 2028-03-20T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private network onboarding — roles, egress IPs, and PrivateLink vs peering evaluation

Thanks Mateo — useful summary. Quick answers from my side:
- Nat/firewall owner: NetOps will own egress NAT and firewall rules. I'll loop in Kevin from NetOps in the next message.
- I'll send a draft allowlist CSV tomorrow (Mar 21) but we may only have ranges, not exact IPs until NetOps approves.
- We prefer PrivateLink if it doesn't require additional formal network peering approvals (we're trying to avoid a lengthy peering PR). If PrivateLink requires us to expose multiple endpoints, that may be heavier than peering — we'll confirm after NetOps review.

We also need an estimate of the per-node egress bandwidth and expected burst patterns for the POC traffic so NetOps can size the interface. Can Ben include that in the peering model vs PrivateLink notes?

Safa
Director, IT Infrastructure | NetBank
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-03-21T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private network onboarding — roles, egress IPs, and PrivateLink vs peering evaluation

Safa — thanks for the quick reply and for confirming NetOps ownership. Ben and I talked through the sizing ask; I'll kick off the runbook and Ben will provide the bandwidth numbers. Short notes below and what I'll deliver by EOD tomorrow: 

What we'll deliver (internal owners):
- Marissa: Draft onboarding runbook (network steps, endpoint testing, connectivity verification checklist), including cloud-side config snippets for PrivateLink and peering.
- Ben: Egress bandwidth estimate, expected concurrent connections, and recommended NAT/elastic IP footprint for the peering model.
- Mateo: Updated procurement timeline and SOW stub for your procurement team.

Conditional items for NetOps to confirm:
- Whether you need dedicated ENIs per PrivateLink endpoint or a shared endpoint is acceptable for the POC (impacts how many allowlist IPs we'll provide).
- Any downstream firewall deep-packet inspection that may require us to use TLS passthrough.

Attachment: updated preflight with a column for "NetOps approver" added so we can track sign-off.

I'll send the runbook draft and the updated preflight by EOD (Mar 21 PST).

— Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Safa Ahmed <safa@netbank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-21T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private network onboarding — roles, egress IPs, and PrivateLink vs peering evaluation

Hi all — Ben here. Per Marissa's note, attaching the quick bandwidth and NAT footprint estimates (excerpt below). Happy to sync with NetOps on a short 30-minute call to walk through numbers.

Excerpt — POC (week of Apr 8) suggested sizing:
- Average token throughput: 50 requests/sec, median response size ~1.2k tokens -> estimated egress ~5-10 Mbps per inference node (steady), burst up to 40-50 Mbps for short tail events.
- Suggested initial footprint: 3 inference nodes for POC (handles concurrency + failover) -> aggregate steady egress 15-30 Mbps, peak ~150 Mbps.
- If NetBank prefers peering + Redwood-managed egress we recommend reserving 4 elastic IPs (NAT) to start; NetOps can tighten once traffic patterns stabilize.

PrivateLink notes:
- If NetBank hosts the interface endpoints we can provide 3 stable IPs (one per AZ) and keep routing ownership entirely with NetOps — minimal changes on Redwood side.
- If PrivateLink requires multiple endpoints per service we can consolidate but we need NetOps approval for how many interface endpoints are acceptable.

Action: Safa/Kevin — if you can propose 2 available 30-minute windows tomorrow (Mar 22) for a quick network sync, I'll join and walk through the numbers + runbook items.

Attachment: netbank-egress-ips.csv (placeholder ranges included)

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
